summary: The root هبو (hbw) describes ashes becoming mixed with dust and extinguishing. It also refers to embers dying out.
lane: 1 هَباَ الرَّمَادُ ذ , (JK, TA,) aor. يَهْبُو , (TA,) The ashes became mixed with dust, and extinguished: (JK, TA:) and هَباَ الجَمْرُ . (M, art. رمد .)

headwords.def: هَباَ الرَّمَادُ, (JK, TA,) aor. يَهْبُو, (TA,) The ashes became mixed with dust, and extinguished: (JK, TA:) and هَباَ الجَمْرُ. (M, art. رمد.)
هَبْوَةٌ Dust rising, or spreading, in the sky like smoke. (JK.)
هَبَآءٌ The motes that are seen in the rays of the sun: (TA:) see an ex. voce غُثَآءٌ.

headword_note: Lane indexes geminate roots with two letters where the Corpus uses three; both spellings are resolved here.
